newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ASMI SEES NO BIG Q2 IMPROVEMENT.
newsitem.headline: ASMI SEES NO BIG Q2 IMPROVEMENT.

text.p: Dutch semiconductor equipment maker ASM International said late on Monday first quarter 1997 earnings dropped, adding that results for the second quarter would not show a substantial improvement.

The company issued a statement late on Monday showing net earnings in the first quarter at 0.4 million guilders, down from 26.8 million a year earlier. Net sales dropped 28 percent to 129.9 million reflecting continued soft market conditions in the semiconductor equipment industry, the firm said.
"The short term outlook remains, however, difficult," the company said in a statement.

"Although the order intake is improving slowly, the results for the second quarter will not show a substantial improvement. This is due to the time needed between order and shipment as most equipment includes customer specifications," it said.
ASM International said it had seen signs of more positive market sentiment at recent trade shows and added that it was confident it would participate fully when a market upturn materialised.

ASM International said markets in the Far East and Japan were stronger than in Europe and in the United States, while new orders exceeded shipments during the quarter, which traditionally sees lower than average activity.
The backlog of firm orders at the end of March stood at 199 million guilders, the company said.
